title: Certificates of Deposit: published standard rates, compounding and day-count basis
content:
## Scope

This rate card covers every tier of the bank's Certificates of Deposit and states the currently published standard rates for a new term, together with the compounding frequency and the day-count basis used for daily interest.

## Terms used on this card

- **Standard APY** is the currently published annual percentage yield for a new term of the tier, before any bonuses, in percent.
- **Standard interest rate** is the currently published interest rate for a new term of the tier, before any bonuses, in percent. It is the rate which, compounded daily, produces the standard APY.
- **Compounding frequency** is how often accrued interest is added to the interest base. It is *daily* on every tier.
- **Day-count basis** is the number of days in the year used to compute daily interest, as a whole number of days.

## Published rate card

| Tier | Standard APY (percent) | Standard interest rate (percent) | Compounding frequency | Day-count basis (days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 3.85 | 3.78 | Daily | 365 |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 3.60 | 3.54 | Daily | 365 |
| 12-Month Certificate | 4.05 | 3.97 | Daily | 365 |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 3.90 | 3.83 | Daily | 365 |
| 36-Month Certificate | 3.55 | 3.49 | Daily | 365 |
| 60-Month Certificate | 3.45 | 3.39 | Daily | 365 |

## Reading the card

**Why is each APY higher than the interest rate beside it?**
Because the standard interest rate is compounded daily, and daily compounding of that rate produces the standard APY. The two figures describe the same published pricing, once as a rate and once as a yield.

**Do these figures include the jumbo or relationship bonus?**
No. Both columns are stated before bonuses.

**Which tier currently carries the highest published APY?**
The 12-Month Certificate, at 4.05 percent. The lowest is the 60-Month Certificate, at 3.45 percent.

**Is the day-count basis ever different between tiers?**
Not at present: every tier uses 365 days, and every tier compounds daily.

## Comparison by term (derived from the card)

| Tier | Gap between standard APY and standard interest rate (percentage points) |
|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 0.07 |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 0.06 |
| 12-Month Certificate | 0.08 |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 0.07 |
| 36-Month Certificate | 0.06 |
| 60-Month Certificate | 0.06 |

The gap is simply the standard APY less the standard interest rate on the same row; it carries no separate pricing meaning.
